newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds keen to push on as Treasuries support.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds keen to push on as Treasuries support.

text.p: German Bund futures freshened up in early trade with a sprint up to 101.13/14 resistance, egged on by a strong performance in the U.S. market after Tuesday's benign inflation data.

But traders said that with volumes likely to be relatively thin ahead of a May Day holiday in Germany on Thursday, and more potentitially dangerous U.S. data due this session, June Bunds might run into difficulties in the 101.20/25 area.
By 0637 GMT, the DTB Bunds was up 17 basis points at 101.17, while the 10-year cash Bunds was offering at 5.801 percent yield at a price of 101.37.

Wednesday's menu of U.S. data includes preliminary first quarter growth numbers and the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index, with economists expecting a slight pick up in economic growth to 4.1 percent from 3.8 percent previously. The big-hitting non-farm payrolls report is also due on Friday.

In the face of that, some analysts warned against being taken in too much by the Bund rally. "The reason Bunds are going up is not domestic. The fundamentals are constructive, but nothing has really changed," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
"Meanwhile we have GDP and the Chicago PMI today and non-farm payrolls on Friday in the U.S. -- both of which could prove to be substantial landmines," he said.

Nevertheless, with the Bund happy to push higher in early business, analysts said the June contact would first try to overcome the 101.20/25 region, before heading for the next critical resiastance point at 101.61, where a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement level kicks in.
"There is nothing for the moment to stop it getting there," said Diebel.

With a convincing rally above the April highs of 101.14 on the June Bund and 108.84 on the Bobl needed first to confirm a succesfful break higher, analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell futures and options said the next substantial target would come in until 102.00 -- the top of the April upchannel plotted on daily charts.

In the cash market, with Treasuries softening slightly in automated trade, the 10-year T-note/Bund yield gap had pushed out to 110 basis points by 0705 GMT as Bunds took back some of the ground lost on Tuesday.
